# Sutram ROUND-92 WS1 — C calls with zero C-runtime dependency (one-page decision)

**Verdict:** **YES**, an executable can call a **freestanding C function** without libc or a dynamic loader. **NO**, it cannot call libc's actual `printf` without linking its implementation (or another equivalent formatter). **Sutram cannot yet do arbitrary C calls**; the native compiler has no foreign-symbol ABI or object linker. Build-time C tools are distinct from a runtime dependency.

## Actually executed control — not generated by Sutram

[Freestanding C function](ROUND-92-WS1-FREESTANDING-C.c): `long sutram_ffi_add(long a,long b) { return a+b; }`. [Raw Linux entry](ROUND-92-WS1-FREESTANDING-ENTRY.S): use x86-64 **SysV C ABI** to call it with 17 and 25, then print through raw `sys_write`. GCC compiled the objects; `ld -nostdlib -static -e _start` linked the executable. **Observed stdout:** `NO_LIBC_C_CALL=42\n`; **exit 42** (intended), 9,096 bytes, **no `PT_INTERP`, dynamic section or `DT_NEEDED` libraries**. The C object has **zero undefined symbols**. Removing it makes the link **FAIL exit 1** with `undefined reference to 'sutram_ffi_add'`. [Exact commands and raw results](ROUND-92-WS1-NOLIBC-OBSERVED.txt). This proves the ABI/link technique, **not a Sutram FFI**.

## Which approaches satisfy the no-runtime contract?

| Mechanism | C-call possible? | External runtime? |
|---|---|---|
| **Static object** from self-contained freestanding C, then native link | **YES, measured** | **None in final ELF**; C compiler/linker are *build-time* tools |
| ELF **PLT/GOT, DT_NEEDED, `PT_INTERP`** | YES | Requires OS **dynamic loader and external shared library**, potentially libc — **not** dependency-free |
| **Statically embed libc `printf`** | YES | No dynamic libc, but **includes substantial libc code** — violates project’s no-C-runtime design |
| Windows **PE import table** | YES for Windows API callable functions | Depends on OS loader/system DLL, **not the C runtime**; current Sutram already imports `KERNEL32.dll` |
| Direct OS syscalls / Windows API wrappers | **Only OS operations**, not arbitrary C | No libc/CRT; per-OS kernel interfaces remain dependencies |

A syscall cannot provide libc `printf`'s parsing, floating formatting, locale and stream behavior automatically. A bounded integer/text formatter plus `write` is a useful *different* API.

## What Sutram would have to implement

An **explicit opt-in, integer/pointer-only foreign declaration and ABI**, no implicit `printf` lookup; link vetted local objects with all undefined dependencies resolved; emit relocatable code and symbol/relocation tables (or a reviewed equivalent static link phase). Current `write_elf` emits `ET_EXEC` without symbols and `backpatch_calls` resolves only Sutram-local functions. Linux SysV and Windows x64 conventions differ. Check symbol hashes, object bounds, relocation types, stack alignment and unsupported C compiler helpers (stack protector, TLS, `libgcc`) before publishing. Preserve default libc-free binary output. **This is compiler/linker architecture work: STOP, no compiler edit this round.**

**Small syscall-only track, immediately more realistic:** file I/O → Linux `openat/read/write/close`, Windows `CreateFileW/ReadFile/WriteFile/CloseHandle`; memory → `mmap/munmap` or `VirtualAlloc/VirtualFree`; time → `clock_gettime` or `QueryPerformanceCounter/GetSystemTimePreciseAsFileTime`. Enforce per-OS error, resource-lifetime and clock semantics. `likha` already handles output; `dvaram` is file-open, **not** a generic FFI. Hand-built Windows imports exist today in `win/pe_imports.inc`; they are system imports, not arbitrary dynamically linked C libraries.

**Statuses:** GNU C-ABI control **PASS**; omitted-object link **EXPECTED FAIL**; no-libc ELF evidence **PASS**; Sutram native foreign call/compiler test **NOT_RUN**; real libc `printf` without libc/formatter **UNAVAILABLE BY DEFINITION**; design **DELIVERED**, implementation **NOT_STARTED**.
